multibayes

multibayes is an R package for making directional claims about several parameters from a Bayesian model, when the number of tests should be taken into account.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mar-cald/multibayes")

What it does

Function Input Output
pd.adjust() Posterior draws, or a vector of pd values For each parameter, the probability of direction (pd) and its value under a more skeptical prior (pd.adj)
joint() Posterior draws Simultaneous credible intervals, or with interval = FALSE the joint probability of the strongest directional claims

pd.adjust()

A direction is usually claimed when pd reaches a threshold such as 0.975. With many parameters, this rule makes more and more wrong claims. pd.adjust() separates two choices.

  • threshold (c, default 0.975) is the posterior probability you require to make a claim. It stays the same whatever the number of tests.
  • pi.max is the largest prior probability you allow for either direction of a parameter. With 0.5 nothing changes. A larger value makes the prior more skeptical about each claim.

pd.adj is the posterior probability of the favored direction when that direction has prior probability 1 - pi.max. A direction is claimed when pd.adj >= c, which is the same as pd >= c*, a larger value shown in the output. The model is not refitted.

To choose pi.max, think of how many effects in the family could be null. That proportion is a reference value. If up to 70% of the effects could be null, at most 30% lie in each direction, so each direction should be allowed a prior probability as low as 0.3, which gives pi.max = 0.7. A larger value gives fewer false claims at a cost in power. The same pi.max is used for every test, so you should be equally skeptical of a claim about any parameter in the family. The parameters can be on different scales. pd.adj remains a probability about the sign of a parameter. It is not the probability that an effect is non-null. Alternatively, p0 sets the largest prior probability that no claim in the family is correct, and pi.max is then p0^(1/m) for m tests.

The prior of the fitted model must be continuous and symmetric about the null value, as flat priors and symmetric priors centred on it are (normal or Student-t priors, for example).

library(multibayes)
draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(4000, mu = c(1, 0.2, 3), Sigma = diag(3))
colnames(draws) <- c("b1", "b2", "b3")

res <- pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi.max = 0.7)
res          # pd, pd.adj, and the thresholds
plot(res)    # range of the posterior probability as the prior changes

joint() 

joint(draws)                     # simultaneous credible intervals
joint(draws, interval = FALSE)   # joint probability of the strongest claims

Simultaneous intervals need more draws as the number of parameters grows. joint() warns when there are too few.

Citation

Calderan, M., Gambarota, F., Finos, L., & Altoè, G. (n.d.). A Prior-Odds Adjustment for the Probability of Direction in Multiple Testing. Retrieved from https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/8zwx2_v2

Run citation("multibayes") in R for the full reference (article and package entries).
